summary: Phase 2b.3: accelerometer threshold detection + per-athlete calibration. New `app/src/phone/motion.ts` ships pure-function impulse detection (`magnitudeG`, `createImpulseDetector(thresholdG, debounceMs)`, `computeCalibrationThreshold(peaks[])` via p10−ε with `CALIBRATION_MIN_THRESHOLD_G = 0.8` floor, `getActiveThresholdG(profile)` as the single-source-of-truth accessor for the per-profile threshold lookup); defaults are `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_G = 1.8 g` / `DEFAULT_DEBOUNCE_MS = 300 ms` / `CALIBRATION_FLOOR_G = 0.5 g` / `CALIBRATION_EPSILON_G = 0.2 g` / `CALIBRATION_SAMPLE_COUNT = 5`. New `app/src/phone/motion-runner.ts` is the mode-aware translator that converts `MotionSample` → `commit` (armed) or `sample` (calibrating) `PhoneMessage`s. Wire format extended with two variants: `{ type: 'sample'; t; peakG }` (phone→laptop calibration peaks) and `{ type: 'config'; thresholdG; debounceMs; mode }` (laptop→phone). `DrillConfig` gains optional `phoneCalibration?: { thresholdG; calibratedAt }` (no Dexie schema bump — field is `??`-faulted). New `app/src/ui/CalibrateScreen.tsx` is mounted inside `PairScreen` when the peer is connected: collects 5 sample peaks via a peer-message subscription, fits the threshold via `computeCalibrationThreshold`, persists to `ProfileRecord.config.phoneCalibration`, and sends `mode: 'armed'` back to the phone. `PhoneApp` adds a 'Motion sensor' section with an iOS-gated `DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission()` path (Android Chrome over HTTP works without prompts per §B4); the listener feeds a `MotionRunner` whose output is forwarded over the DataChannel. `PairScreen` loads the active profile alongside settings, sends an initial `mode: 'armed'` config the moment the DataChannel opens, and mounts `CalibrateScreen` when `peerState === 'connected'`. New `docs/SETUP_IOS.md` documents the mkcert HTTPS walkthrough (per §B4 — iOS is doc-driven, not CI-gated). New `app/verify-phase-2b3.mjs` ships C1+C2 gate-grade UI checks (motion section renders + Enable-click flips to status='on') plus C3 best-effort (calibration panel renders when peer is connected — §B2 documented limitation) and M1–M8 manual-QA checklist. 33 new vitest tests (180 total, was 147 baseline): 18 motion (impulse threshold, exact debounce-boundary, 60s-rest, single + five-impulse + double-tap acceptance criteria, calibration p10 vs `min` at length 11, floor clamp, `getActiveThresholdG`), 5 motion-runner (armed/calibrating mode messages, setConfig reset, mode exposure), 8 wire (sample + config round-trips, NaN/Infinity/zero/negative threshold rejection, negative debounce rejection, unknown-mode rejection, missing-field rejection), 2 profiles (calibration round-trip, overwrite). Lint + tsc + vite build all clean. Bundle: main bundle UNCHANGED at 344.22 KB / 106.44 KB gzip (Phase 2b.2 baseline 344.20 / 106.45 — the +0 KB main-bundle preservation continues); PairScreen chunk 139.98 KB / 51.04 KB gzip (+3.09 KB raw / +0.87 KB gzip for CalibrateScreen, inside the lazy boundary); PhoneApp chunk 7.57 KB / 2.70 KB gzip (+3.16 KB raw / +1.03 KB gzip for motion + motion-runner, also inside its lazy boundary). Code-reviewer (`code-reviewer` agent) returned REQUEST-CHANGES with 2 blockers + 4 should-fix + 4 nits; blockers and the four cheap fixes (DRY accessor, `Date.now()`→`performance.now()`, debounce-boundary test, percentile test) plus three nits (NaN/Infinity guard on config, `MotionRunner.config` defensive copy, the debounce + percentile tests) were applied before approval. Findings deferred with rationale: #5 `finishCalibration` re-binds listener on profile update — currently harmless because status immediately transitions to 'done' after onSaved (reviewer agreed); #6 `peer.send` failure during `startCalibration` — the phone's default mode is 'armed', so a failed switch to 'calibrating' correctly leaves the phone in its prior armed state (the audit was wrong about the symmetry: there is no prior 'calibrating' state the phone could be stuck in). Phase 2b.3 motion + DataChannel paths are gated by the manual_qa checklist M1–M8 in `artifacts/phase-2b3-verify/results.json` per the §B2 concession; the autonomous loop cannot perform real-device accelerometer QA, so M1–M8 are recorded as `pending operator sign-off` in the approval artifact's manual_qa block.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 60s at rest on a flat surface → 0 commit events received by the laptop
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: motion.test.ts 'emits zero commits across a still 60-second baseline' feeds 60×60 zero-magnitude samples to createImpulseDetector at the default threshold and asserts zero commits; would fail if the threshold check were removed. M1 in the manual_qa block re-verifies the same property on real hardware where the at-rest accelerometer has noise.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 5 deliberate forward-snap impulses → exactly 5 commit events received
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: motion.test.ts 'emits exactly five commits for five well-separated impulses' (800 ms apart, well clear of the 300 ms debounce). M2 in manual_qa re-verifies on a real phone with the laptop debug surface counting commits.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Double-snap within 300ms debounce window → exactly 1 commit event
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: motion.test.ts 'debounces a double-tap within the debounce window to one commit' (impulses at 100 ms and 250 ms — gap 150 ms < 300 ms debounce). The strict-less-than boundary semantics is pinned by 'admits an impulse at exactly the debounce-window boundary' so a future +/- comparison flip would fail. M3 in manual_qa re-verifies on real hardware.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Calibration: 5 sample swings → threshold persists across page reload; re-running calibration overwrites prior value
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: computeCalibrationThreshold tested for default-fallback (empty array → DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_G), p10−ε behavior at length 5 (smallest = p10) and length 11 (second-smallest = p10, pinning that this is not Math.min), and minimum-floor clamp. Storage round-trip + overwrite tested in profiles.test.ts: 'round-trips a phoneCalibration field on the profile config' and 'overwrites the prior phoneCalibration on re-save'. M4/M5/M6 in manual_qa re-verify the end-to-end UI flow on real hardware: start → 5 swings → saved threshold → reload → still saved → re-run with different swings → overwrites.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `phone/motion.ts` is pure-function unit-tested with synthesized accel streams
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: motion.test.ts (18 tests) covers magnitudeG (zero vector, single-axis, 3-4-5-triangle norm), createImpulseDetector (still baseline, single impulse, five impulses, double-tap within debounce, exact-boundary debounce, post-debounce re-fire, below-threshold ignored, reset() clears debounce), computeCalibrationThreshold (empty, p10−ε at length 5, length 11 percentile-vs-min, re-run differs, min-floor clamp), getActiveThresholdG (calibrated, missing, null/undefined profile). The pure module has zero browser-API dependencies — vitest runs it under jsdom without sensor mocks per QUALITY_GATES.md §'Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b)'.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: `docs/SETUP_IOS.md` documents the mkcert path; iOS acceptance is doc-driven, not CI-gated
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: docs/SETUP_IOS.md (new) walks through mkcert install (macOS + Linux), LAN-IP cert generation, iOS root-CA install + Certificate Trust Settings toggle (the step iOS users most often miss), Vite --https serving (dev + preview), and troubleshooting (cert warnings, requestPermission gestures, expired certs, IP changes). Acceptance per §B4 — iOS support is shipped as a documented path, not a CI gate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Android Chrome over plain HTTP: works without permission prompts
acceptance_criteria.verified_by: PhoneApp.handleEnableMotion calls DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission ONLY when the API exposes that method (iOS-specific); on Android Chrome the typeof check is false, so the listener attaches without any permission prompt. M7 in manual_qa re-verifies on a real Android device.

verify-phase-2b3.mjs runs C1+C2 gate-grade automated checks (motion section renders with the 'Enable motion sensor' button and status='off'; click → status='on' with zero console errors) plus a C3 best-effort check (calibration panel renders when peer is connected — best-effort because headless chromium without UDP cannot reach 'connected'). Eight-item M1–M8 manual_qa_checklist is written to artifacts/phase-2b3-verify/results.json for operator sign-off. Current automated run: C1+C2 PASS (gate-grade), C3 FAIL (best-effort — same documented WebRTC/ICE limitation as 2b.1 C5 and 2b.2 C2/C4 per §B2), console_errors=0.

playwright_run.automated_gate_checks: C1, C2 PASS — /phone renders the Motion sensor section with status='off' and an 'Enable motion sensor' button + the manual 'Send commit (manual)' button (no regression in the 2b.1 manual escape hatch); clicking Enable flips status to 'on' (or 'unsupported' if DeviceMotionEvent is absent in the agent) within 5 s, with zero console errors.
playwright_run.best_effort_calibration_panel: C3 FAIL — Pair view's CalibrateScreen panel only renders when peerState === 'connected', which headless chromium without UDP/STUN typically cannot reach. Same documented expected outcome as 2b.1's C5 and 2b.2's C2/C4 per QUALITY_GATES.md §'Browser-API limitations (Phase 2b)' and the §B2 concession; manual M4–M6 are the authoritative gate for the calibration flow.

M2 — Five deliberate forward-snap impulses → laptop shows EXACTLY 5 new commits.

manual_qa.operator_sign_off_instructions: Update artifacts/phase-2b3-verify/results.json — set each entry's `signed_off` to {date:'YYYY-MM-DD', device:'<phone model + OS>', laptop_camera:'(n/a — motion, not camera)'} after exercising the step on a real LAN+phone pair. The §B2 concession requires this field to be populated before the phase can be considered fully closed; the autonomous loop cannot perform real-device accelerometer QA, so the operator sign-off is the human's role in this gate. gates.testing: 180/180 vitest tests pass (Phase 2b.2 baseline was 147; +33 new). Every new public branch in motion.ts, motion-runner.ts, the wire-format extension, and the profile-storage extension has at least one would-fail-if-reverted test. The debounce boundary is pinned by an exact-DEBOUNCE-MS test; the calibration percentile is pinned by a length-11 test that the implementation passes and a `Math.min` regression would fail. UI state machines and DeviceMotion handshakes are gated by manual real-device QA per the §B2 concession recorded in QUALITY_GATES.md and addressed in the manual_qa block above.

DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_G`. PhoneApp's initial runner uses DEFAULT_THRESHOLD_G directly (no profile context at construction time — it learns the per-athlete threshold from the laptop's first `config` message). Wire-format constants live in wire.ts only; motion constants live in motion.ts only.

review.code_reviewer: REQUEST-CHANGES on the implementation. 2 blockers + 4 should-fix + 4 nits. Blockers + cheap fixes applied: (#1) PhoneApp motion-listener leak in the manual flow APPLIED (added an unconditional cleanup useEffect; the QR-flow effect early-returns in manual pairing and cannot own teardown); (#2) CalibrateScreen setPeaks updater double-firing finishCalibration under StrictMode APPLIED (introduced peaksRef as the authoritative store; the message handler runs once per delivered message, immune to StrictMode's updater double-invoke); (#3) DRY accessor for the active threshold APPLIED (`getActiveThresholdG(profile)` in motion.ts; PairScreen and CalibrateScreen both use it); (#4) Date.now()→performance.now() in toMotionSample APPLIED (monotonic clock guarantees s.t − lastCommitAt is non-negative under NTP/DST jumps); (#7) exact-debounce-boundary test APPLIED; (#8) length-11 calibration percentile test APPLIED (pins p10 ≠ min); (#9) isPhoneMessage NaN/Infinity/zero/negative guards APPLIED; (#10) MotionRunner.config defensive copy APPLIED. Findings deferred with rationale: (#5) finishCalibration listener re-bind on profile update — reviewer agreed it is currently harmless because the status transitions to 'done' before any re-bind matters; the ref-based fix is a refactor without an observable bug; (#6) peer.send failure on startCalibration — the audit assumed a prior 'calibrating' state, but the phone's default mode is 'armed' and only 'calibrating' is ever sent inside startCalibration, so a failed send correctly leaves the phone armed (no inconsistent state to recover from).
